messages:
sarah_ae: Customer: must see original client IP in L3 source for every request (siem correlation). They explicitly refuse header-based attribution. Can we do that for a Private deploy?
sean_net: Short: yes, but only if traffic is routed (L3) to Redwood without SNAT in the path. That rules out patterns that terminate/proxy at a shared public edge.
lisa_sales: Any quick recommendation for a POC that we can stand up in ~2 weeks?
tom_arch: Fastest path if they control the cloud side: deploy an NLB or ENI-based L4 forwarder in the customer's VPC that forwards traffic over a routed VPN/DirectConnect to our private infra. With that, src IP is preserved end-to-end.
sean_net: Alternative: Transit Gateway attachment + static routes from customer VPCs to Redwood VPCs. Must ensure no NAT on any hop. Works well for multi-account setups.
maria_sec: Security caveat: preserving client IP means potentially carrying external src IPs into our infra. We need a signed attestation from customer that they accept IP provenance/abuse risk and a logging retention agreement. Also require strict ACLs and IDS on customer edge.
sean_net: If customer wants AWS-native: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) will not preserve client source IP because traffic is sent to interface ENIs — original source becomes the endpoint ENI. Same for API Gateway/LB sinks. So PrivateLink alone won't meet "true" src-ip requirement.
lisa_sales: So if they request PrivateLink for compliance, it's a mismatch?
tom_arch: Correct. PrivateLink -> header only. For real src-ip we need routed connectivity (VPC peering, TGW, or DX/VPN).
sean_net: POC checklist (send to their network ops):
```
- Connectivity method: choose one: Site-to-Site VPN (IPSec) OR Direct Connect with private VIF OR Transit Gateway peering.
- Routing: advertise customer prefixes to Redwood; Redwood will advertise service prefixes back. Avoid any SNAT on the forwarding path.
- Ports/protocols: allow TCP 443 outbound from customer edge to Redwood CIDR 10.210.0.0/22; allow return traffic. For IPSec: UDP 500/4500 and ESP (proto 50).
- BGP: if using DX, configure BGP neighbors. Confirm ASNs and prefix filters.
- MTU: ensure MTU >= 1400; if using GRE/GWLB adjust PMTU.
- Whitelist Redwood service egress IPs for control-plane: 34.198.45.0/24 (example).
- Health checks: allow TCP 443 and TCP 10256 (agent) to the service subnet.
- NO SNAT anywhere along the path that touches Redwood subnets.
```
sean_net: POC infra notes: we'll request a dedicated route table and a route propagation entry so customer prefixes route to our attachment. If using TGW, attach a dedicated route table for the POC.
maria_sec: Also: require mutually authenticated IPSec or DX + BGP with MD5 for session integrity. Logging MUST be enabled on customer edge and firewall.
lisa_sales: Pricing & timeline?
tom_arch: Pricing: small monthly surcharge for a routed dedicated attachment (covers reserved capacity + IP allocation) + standard egress. For POC we can cover the attachment infra; customer covers data egress. Estimate: 2-3 engineer-days to configure routing, 1 day to validate, so plan ~5 working days if they have VPN/DX ready. If they need Direct Connect provisioning, add lead time (weeks).
sarah_ae: Can we offer a fallback so the app stays up if routed path flaps?
sean_net: We recommend dual-path: primary = routed path (preserve src), secondary = PrivateLink with header fallback. Must document in SOW that during fallback attribution will be header-based and not L3.
lisa_sales: I'll package the checklist + dual-path SOW language and ask for their network contact + whether they can open a TAC case for DX.
maria_sec: I'll prepare the minimal legal logging addendum for IP retention and acceptance.
infra-bot: infra-bot: created ticket RDW-POC-3215 for routed-poc; assignees: sean_net, tom_arch.
sean_net: OK sending to customer now. Short next steps: (1) confirm connectivity option (VPN/DX/TGW), (2) obtain customer edge IPs & ASN, (3) get signoff on logging addendum.
lisa_sales: Thanks everyone, sharing now. :thumbsup:
